regime_context: The detector shows a broad, non-one-narrative US regime with Memory/HBM as the eligible leader (score 3.05) but modest durability (0.44) and zero breadth, while Silver and Gold Miners sit close behind with full breadth and high durability — a leadership handoff toward precious metals is arguably more CONFIRMED than the AI/memory complex's hold. Rotation breadth is wide (73% eligible) with low absorption (0.32) and no directional one-narrative, so this is a choppy multi-theme tape, not a single-trend regime. The one validated edge (absolute-trend gate) is intact here; rank-IC is still a focus lens only.
emerging_watch: Watch whether the precious-metals complex (Gold + Silver Miners) overtakes Memory/HBM as the CONFIRMED leader — the rotation margin is already narrow (1.035) and Gold's breadth/durability is vastly superior. The observable I'm watching: GDX and SIL both posting a higher score than memory_storage in a single subsequent detector reading, which would retire this watch and confirm the handoff.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners (GDX) is the cleanest trend-gate-and-durability combination in the entire ranks: eligible, Hurst 'trend', durability_bar 0.84 (one of the highest), breadth 1.0 (every constituent participating), and crowding_z only 0.55 (not extended). Unlike the headline leader (Memory, breadth 0.0, durability 0.44, 'fading'), GDX shows confirmed, broad, durable trend structure — this is exactly the pattern the validated absolute-trend gate was designed to stay with, and the rotation leg confirms a precious-metals complex rising as the semiconductor narrative fades.
evidence: hurst_tag='trend' vs 'mixed/fading' for the AI complex
breadth=1.0 — all names participating, not a single-stock move
eligible=true and crowding_z=0.55 (not a sizing-down caution)
rotation.challenger/leader gap: Silver (rank 2) and Gold (rank 3) are the only names within 1.2 score of the fading leader
theses.dissent: Miners are a high-beta play on real yields and the USD; if the macro backdrop is really 'ai_tech dominant' with unscheduled_share 0.89, a sudden AI-led risk-on rally could crush the miners' relative edge in days — and Gold Miners have historically gapped down hard in single-session risk events.

falsifier.text: GDX lags SPY by 6% over any rolling 15-day window inside the horizon before rallying to a new 60-day high

theses.subject: Silver Miners
theses.thesis: Silver Miners (SIL) mirrors the Gold trade with even more torque: eligible, breadth 1.0, durability 0.79, mixed Hurst but positive score (2.015) and only rank 2. The precious-metals complex as a whole is the only broad-based, high-durability leadership on the board while the AI/memory front-runners are narrow and fading. Lean overweight as a companion to GDX only — not a standalone call, because Silver's mixed Hurst and lower score mean less staying-power evidence than Gold.
evidence: hurst_tag='mixed' — trend not yet as locked-in as Gold's 'trend'
theses.dissent: Silver is the industrial precious metal; if the detector's 'ai_tech' macro backdrop means strong industrial demand is priced in and then misses, SIL's industrial beta could undercut the monetary-precious case and lag GDX badly.

falsifier.text: SIL underperforms GDX by 8% over the horizon while both rise

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: Memory/HBM is the rank-1 leader but the detector's own legs argue against chasing it: breadth 0.0 (leadership is extremely narrow), durability_bar 0.44 (lowest of any top-5 eligible name), Hurst 'mixed', and val_state 'fading' in the headline. The trend gate is 'validated risk control' not a return signal, and this leader lacks the breadth/durability signature that the gate rewards. Avoid is a de-risk stance, not a fade/short — and consistent with guardrails that forbid fading the leader on reflexivity grounds.
evidence: guardrails.do_not_conclude: rank is a focus lens, not a buy list; do not chase on momentum
theses.dissent: This could be a false fade — single-name HBM momentum (e.g. a memory pricing cycle turn) can re-accelerate violently before breadth catches up, and the score 3.05 is by far the strongest on the board; avoiding the top-ranked name could leave the desk underweight the actual next leg.

falsifier.text: SMH makes a new 60-day high with breadth in the Memory/HBM group above 0.5 before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
